body:
OBSERVED in source, 2026-08-23. Runtime confirmation of the queues themselves is ASSUMED — the
seed instance had nothing scheduled, so I saw the classic tables render empty, not populated.

Classic's Tasks page carries two admin-only queues besides the running-task table:
"Upcoming scheduled sends" (`cps/templates/tasks.html:31-50`) and "Upcoming scheduled
operations" (`cps/templates/tasks.html:53-75`), each showing scheduled time and state with a
cancel action. The SPA's Tasks page (`frontend/src/pages/Tasks.tsx`) renders only the running
worker queue.

This is NOT the scheduled-task *editor* — that gap is counted separately. These are
observation-and-cancellation surfaces, and losing them means an admin cannot see or stop
already-scheduled work from the new UI.

The data already exists as JSON, admin-gated:
- `GET  /cwa-scheduled/upcoming`      -> `{"items": [...]}`  (`cps/cwa_functions.py:1736-1748`)
- `GET  /cwa-scheduled/upcoming-ops`  -> `{"items": [...]}`  (`cps/cwa_functions.py:1750-1764`)
- `POST /cwa-scheduled/cancel`                               (`cps/cwa_functions.py:699-736`)

They live on the `cwa_stats` blueprint rather than `/api/v1`, so this needs a thin API surface
plus the SPA tables — larger than F-57c90e, and it is the piece that actually blocks calling the
new Tasks page a replacement.

Consequence for the retirement audit: surface 54 (Tasks) is Partial, not Native. The audit notes
recorded it as Native with only schedule *editing* carved out, which understated the gap.
title: New UI Tasks has no equivalent of classic's two scheduled-work queues
